newsitem.title: USA: CSCE sugar called to open mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: CSCE sugar called to open mostly unchanged.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were called to open mostly unchanged Friday, dealers said.

But follow-through buying could carry the benchmark October contract over its recent high of 11.58 cents a lb. Producer selling is likely to keep the move below firmer resistance pegged at 11.87 cents, however.
Support in October remained at the recent low of 11.32 cents.

In fundamental news, the Russian sugar beet harvest should equal or surpass that of last year, Agriculture Minister Viktor Khystun said. He did not provide details of the current harvest. Last year, Russia produced 16.1 million tonnes of beet sugar.

Hungary said it will not export sugar in 1997 after losses from exports the previous year. In rump Yugoslavia, sugar production is expected to meet domestic needs with surplus for exporting, Belgrade daily Politika said.
Wednesday, October sugar settled up 0.06 cent at 11.55 cents after trading from 11.57 to 11.48 cents. The rest ended 0.01 to 0.06 firmer.
In London, white sugar futures were higher in light trade Friday. At 0838 EDT/1238 GMT, LIFFE October was up $1.00 to $325.20 and the rest of the board was trading 60 and 70 cents higher.
